body:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/voodootikigod/adlc/issues/378

Problem: `.adlc/manifest.jsonl` predates HMAC signing — signing was introduced partway through the ledger's life (the first signed entry is seq 96; seq 1-95 were written before ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY existed and are legitimately unsigned). `packages/gate-manifest/bin/gate-manifest.mjs` calls `verify(flags.dir)` with no options, so it always runs with the default `requireSignatures: true`. Whenever ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY is present in the environment, that mode requires EVERY entry — including the honest pre-signing prefix — to carry a valid signature, and fails closed at seq 1 every time. This makes the Stop hook (plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs `manifest()`, and the Cursor/opencode equivalents) report 'evidence chain INVALID' on every single session, training users to ignore a signal that should mean real tampering.

`packages/gate-manifest/lib/verify.mjs` already implements and documents `requireSignatures:false` ('tolerate entries with NO sig (legacy/unsigned history) ... A PRESENT-but-invalid sig is STILL rejected'), but the CLI (`gate-manifest verify`) never exposes or passes that flag, so the lenient path this repo actually needs is unreachable.

Scoping decision (resolve during implementation, do not guess silently): blanket-tolerating ANY unsigned entry anywhere in the chain is too permissive — it would let an attacker append a new unsigned entry after the last legitimately-unsigned one and still pass. The lenient mode should only tolerate a missing signature on an entry that precedes the first entry in the file that carries a signature (i.e. a genuinely contiguous legacy prefix). Once the scan reaches the first signed entry, every subsequent entry (signed-era) must carry a valid signature — missing OR invalid both fail the chain from that point forward. An entry with a PRESENT-but-invalid signature must fail verification regardless of position (legacy prefix or signed era) — that is forgery-after-the-fact, never tolerated.

What to build:
1. In `packages/gate-manifest/lib/verify.mjs`, replace the blanket `requireSignatures` boolean's missing-signature tolerance with the scoped rule above: an entry may lack a `sig` field ONLY if no earlier entry in the file carried one (i.e. it is part of the unbroken legacy prefix). Keep the existing behavior that a PRESENT-but-invalid signature always breaks the chain, at any position. Preserve the existing JSDoc contract style and keep `signed:true` semantics meaning 'a key was present and every checked entry that carries or is required to carry a sig verified'.
2. In `packages/gate-manifest/bin/gate-manifest.mjs`, add a `--allow-legacy-unsigned` flag to the `verify` verb that enables the scoped-lenient mode (equivalent to today's `requireSignatures:false`, now re-scoped per point 1). Default (no flag) keeps today's strict behavior for callers that want it (e.g. an explicit forge-from-scratch check). Update the usage string.
3. Update the Stop-hook callers to pass `--allow-legacy-unsigned` (or the equivalent programmatic option) so day-to-day sessions do not false-positive on this repo's own history, while still catching a genuinely broken/forged/truncated chain:
   - `plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/adlc-hook.mjs` (`manifest()` / `runAdlc(['gate-manifest', 'verify', '--json'])`)
   - `plugins/adlc-cursor/hooks/adlc-stop.mjs`
   - `plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/session-hooks.mjs`
4. Update `packages/gate-manifest/README.md` to document the new flag and the scoped-legacy-prefix semantics (the current text describes the old unscoped `requireSignatures:false` behavior).

Acceptance criteria:
- AC1: `node packages/gate-manifest/bin/gate-manifest.mjs verify --json --allow-legacy-unsigned` run against THIS repo's real `.adlc/manifest.jsonl` (with ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY set) returns `valid:true`. Verify by running the exact command in the worktree and inspecting the JSON output.
- AC2: A unit test in `packages/gate-manifest/test/` constructs a synthetic manifest with an unsigned prefix (seq 1-2) followed by signed entries (seq 3+), verifies with `--allow-legacy-unsigned`/`requireSignatures` scoped-lenient mode, and asserts `valid:true`.
- AC3: A unit test constructs a synthetic manifest where an entry AFTER the first signed entry is unsigned (a new unsigned entry appended post-adoption), verifies with the scoped-lenient mode, and asserts `valid:false` with a message identifying that seq/line — proving the scoping is enforced, not a blanket bypass.
- AC4: A unit test constructs a synthetic manifest where a legacy-prefix entry (before the first signed entry) carries a PRESENT-but-WRONG signature, verifies with the scoped-lenient mode, and asserts `valid:false` — proving tampering is still caught even in the lenient legacy prefix.
- AC5: A unit test confirms the strict default (no `--allow-legacy-unsigned` / `requireSignatures:true`) is unchanged: run against a manifest with a genuine legacy unsigned prefix and assert it still returns `valid:false` at the first unsigned entry (protects existing callers that rely on today's strict semantics).
- AC6: `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/` passes (or the repo's equivalent test runner for this package).
- AC7: Manually exercise the Stop hook path — run the updated `manifest()` function (or its CLI invocation) against this repo's real ledger with ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY set, and confirm no 'evidence chain INVALID' system message is emitted.
- AC8: `packages/gate-manifest/README.md` describes the new flag and the scoped-prefix rule; no longer describes the old unscoped 'any unsigned entry anywhere is OK' semantics as current behavior.

This touches an enforcement package (packages/gate-manifest/) and Stop-hook trust surfaces, so it is TRUST-ROOT tier for the cross-model prosecute gate — plan for a distinct-provider adversarial review and a signed cross-model attestation before merge, same as issue #370.
title: gate-manifest verify: tolerate the repo's legacy unsigned manifest prefix without weakening tamper detection
